findings.claim: The docs describe a `SurrogateType` option that this change does not implement. doc/analyzers/MsgPack022.md and the README analyzer index show `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter(SurrogateType = typeof(...))]` and title MsgPack022 "Surrogate member does not match the formatted type". But `GeneratedMessagePackFormatterAttribute` has no members, and the MsgPack022 descriptor and AnalyzerReleases.Unshipped.md use the title "Serialized member must be public and read-write". A user who follows the documented example gets a compile error.

receipt_plan.detail: Compile `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter(SurrogateType = typeof(S))] partial class F : IMessagePackFormatter<T>;` against head-built MessagePack.Annotations. Expect CS0246 or CS0117 for `SurrogateType`, which proves the documented example cannot compile. Separately, diff the MsgPack022 title in doc/analyzers/index.md against `SerializedMemberNotSupported.title`.

findings.claim: Contractless mode serializes only public read-write members, and a class needs an accessible parameterless constructor (otherwise NoDeserializingConstructor is reported). MessagePack's contractless behaviour also covers public get-only members, with deserialization through a matching constructor. So an immutable Project A type with `public int X { get; }` and a constructor is rejected. A type that also has a parameterless constructor silently loses its get-only members, and can serialize as an empty map.

receipt_plan.detail: Take a type `public class P { public P() {} public int X { get; } = 5; public int Y { get; set; } }` with no attributes. Serialize it with ContractlessStandardResolver and with the head-generated `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` formatter, then compare bytes: the generated formatter omits X. Also run the generator on a class that has only `P(int x)` and observe the NoDeserializingConstructor diagnostic.

findings.claim: Contractless mode ignores `[IgnoreMember]` and `[IgnoreDataMember]`. `CreateContractlessMembers` takes every public read-write member without checking ignore attributes, so a member that T explicitly marks as ignored is still serialized. This breaks the criterion "If T does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured".

receipt_plan.detail: Define a Project A type without `[DataContract]` that has `[IgnoreDataMember] public string Secret { get; set; }` plus `public int Id { get; set; }`. Run the generator for a `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` class and assert the generated formatter text does not contain `Secret`. It fails on head.

findings.claim: `[MessagePackFormatter]` attributes on T's members (and on T itself) are not honoured. `CreateMember` always sets `CustomFormatter: null`, so a member with a custom formatter is written with the default resolver formatter. Its bytes then differ from the dynamic or attributed behaviour the criterion "If T does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured" requires.

receipt_plan.detail: Use a `[MessagePackObject]` type with `[Key(0)][MessagePackFormatter(typeof(MyIntFormatter))] public int A { get; set; }`. Serialize it with DynamicObjectResolver and with the head-generated `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` formatter, then compare bytes. They differ because the custom formatter is ignored.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: 'Contractless behaviour over public members' means only public, read-write instance properties and fields are serialized, under string keys. Get-only members are skipped. A class must have an accessible parameterless constructor, and no constructor parameters are matched. This is what `CreateContractlessMembers` / `IsPublicReadWrite` and the NoDeserializingConstructor check in GeneratedFormatterCollector implement.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: 'Contractless behaviour' means the same member and constructor rules as MessagePack's ContractlessStandardResolver. All public readable instance members, including get-only properties, are serialized, and members marked `[IgnoreMember]` or `[IgnoreDataMember]` are skipped. Deserialization picks a public constructor whose parameters match member names and passes them as `constructorParameters`. Minimal edit: in `CreateContractlessMembers`, filter on public readable members instead of `IsPublicReadWrite` and skip ignore-attributed members. Set `IsWritable` from the actual setter. Replace the parameterless-constructor-only check with constructor matching that fills `ObjectSerializationInfo.Create(constructorParameters: ...)`.
